描述_ZN: Snow in the Sky Mountains, Qing Dynasty, by Hua Yan, on paper, color on canvas, 159.1 cm long and 52.8 cm wide.　　Hua Yan's figure paintings are characterized by their distinctive forms, which are distinguished by their distinctive personalities and intrinsic charm. The Snowy Mountains in the Sky is a representative work from his later years.　　Traveling to the frontier was one of Hua Yan's frequent subjects. The present painting depicts a poetic vision of the Tang people traveling to the frontier. In this painting, a single traveler, clad in a large red cloak and hiding a sword, walks slowly through the snow and ice with an old bactrian camel at the foot of the Tianshan Mountains. The sky is gray, the field is empty, the road is long and snow-capped. A lone goose skims the air, and the traveler and the old camel look up at the scene, which seems to have aroused a thousand thoughts of the wanderer. The painting is a blend of scenes and ambiguities. The composition of the painting is long and narrow, creating a visual effect of the sky and the sky, in order to set off the lonely inner world of the characters. The color scheme is elegant, and the matching of colors and the contrast of warm and cold tones are very elaborate. The figures and the old camel are realistically portrayed with exaggerated techniques, and the forward motion of the figures and the humane expression of the old camel make the theme more prominent. The work shows the artist's unique artistic conception and outstanding painting talent.　　The painting is self-referential: "Snow in the Tianshan Mountains. In the spring of Yihai, Xinluo Shanren wrote this in the Studio of the Sound of Talking, at the age of seventy or four." Inscription: "Huayan" at the bottom and "Empty Dust Poetry and Painting" at the lower right corner.
